hero.title: Ashoka and the Mauryan Decline
hero.description: An analytical study of Ashoka’s Dhamma, his administrative policies, and the structural factors leading to the Mauryan disintegration.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Major milestones from Ashoka's accession to the fall of the empire.

cards.details: Reign of Ashoka. Kalinga War (261 BCE) serves as the turning point for Dhamma-Ghosha.
Succession of weak rulers (Kunala, Dasharatha, Samprati) leading to imperial fragmentation.
Assassination of Brihadratha by Pushyamitra Shunga, ending the Mauryan dynasty.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics for Prelims
mnemonics.description: Memorizing the pillars of policy and decline.

items.title: D.A.M.P.
items.decryption: Use this to recall the four pillars of Ashokan governance: D-Dhamma, A-Administrative reforms (Dhamma-Mahamattas), M-Mauryan central control, P-Post-Ashokan succession issues.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming Ashoka abandoned the army after Kalinga; he maintained it for security but favored non-aggression.
Confusing 'Dhamma' with Buddhism; Dhamma was an ethical code for social harmony, distinct from the tenets of Buddha.
Attributing the fall of the empire solely to Ashoka's pacifism, ignoring economic and succession structural failures.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Pataliputra as the Core
  • Expansion to Deccan (Maski/Brahmagiri)
  • Frontiers: Taxila & Ujjain

Personalities

  • Ashoka: The Philosopher King
  • Upagupta: The Buddhist Mentor
  • Brihadratha: The Last Ruler

The Mindmap of Decline

  • Economic Pressure: Heavy military expenditure
  • Succession Crisis: Division between Western and Eastern wings
  • Weak Centralization: Provinces became autonomous
  • Brahminical Reaction: Pushyamitra Shunga's revolt
